Subject: Edge control/data contracts — deployment readout & next steps

Hi Sara / EdgeOps team,

Thanks for carving out time. Per our sync this morning, attaching a compact readout: the diagram in edge-control-data-contracts-v1.drawio.png and a CSV that enumerates the proposed zone-to-zone ACLs (network-zone-table.csv).

Goal for this thread: align on the control/data interface contract for the private VPC deployment (what lives in customer VPC vs. what we manage in the edge zone), confirm TLS termination, and agree on the minimal firewall rules for initial cutover.

Quick agenda:
- Scope: which services are in-customer vs. edge-managed
- Control plane traffic (auth, metrics, configs) vs. data plane (inference requests, KV cache flows)
- TLS termination options and mutual auth for internal services
- Egress constraints / NAT / logging requirements
- Delivery: action owners and target dates (cutover window proposal attached)

Proposed immediate asks:
1) Sara: confirm any company-side firewall or proxy gating that will block 443 egress to our edge control endpoints (list is in the CSV).
2) EdgeOps: review attachment and flag compatibility concerns for the proposed TLS approach (we called out two options in the diagram).
3) Irene / Marcus: create baseline infra/Jira ticket with required sub-tasks so we can hand off to ops next week.

I can host a 30 min follow-up tomorrow if we need a quick decision on TLS termination.

Thanks,
Logan

Subject: Re: Edge control/data contracts — deployment readout & next steps

Thanks Logan — good summary. A few notes from the Nimbus side after a quick read-through: 

- We currently have a strict egress baseline: only outbound 443 to a curated allowlist is permitted. I attached the existing policy (nimbus-firewall-egress-policy.pdf). We'll need the definitive list of FQDNs/IPs and cert pinning guidance before security approves the cutover.
- On TLS termination: we prefer TLS to remain end-to-end to the edge service (our side does not terminate client TLS) and we want mutual TLS between our fronting proxy and Redwood edge for control traffic. That implies we cannot have an edge device terminate client TLS unless mutual-auth is preserved upstream.
- For auditing: our compliance team requires request-level metadata (client_id, request_id) to be forwarded in headers and mirrored to our log collector (S3 bucket). Can Redwood publish the header map you expect?

Question: in your diagram the control plane uses an internal bootstrap endpoint (control.redwood-internal.global). Will that be accessible over the same peered path as inference traffic or is it in a separate management path? We need to understand routing to update our ACLs.

Happy to hop on the call tomorrow afternoon — I can bring our security engineer if needed.

Sara Klein
Head of Cloud Infrastructure, NimbusCloud
sara.klein@nimbuscloud.com
(Upcoming: joining on call with compliance)

Attachment:
- nimbus-firewall-egress-policy.pdf (PDF)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@nimbuscloud.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge control/data contracts — deployment readout & next steps

Sara — great questions, thanks. A few clarifications and proposed action items below.

TL;DR: we can support end-to-end TLS and mTLS for control channels. We recommend the following as an initial deployable contract:

Option A (preferred for security/compliance):
- Client TLS stays end-to-end to Redwood edge ingress. Edge ingress performs SNI-based routing and forwards a preserved TLS tunnel to the inference worker over an encrypted internal link (mutual TLS between edge and worker).
- Control plane (metrics, config) uses a separate mTLS channel authenticated with customer-provided certs (mutual auth).

Option B (simpler routing, more ops overhead):
- Edge terminates client TLS, re-establishes TLS to worker. Requires cert provisioning on edge and careful cert rotation.

Answers to your specific asks: 
- FQDN/IP list: we'll produce a minimal allowlist for cutover. Initial set is 6 FQDNs (control.* and edge.*) + a small set of collector endpoints. I'll post the list to the Drive folder and attach to JIRA.
- Header map: see the snippet below for required headers we will emit. We will not overwrite x-request-id if provided; we will mirror it. (Header map file: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2b_edge-control-readout)

Proposed next steps and owners: 
1) Irene: publish allowlist + header map to Drive by EOD Friday (done).
2) Logan: confirm DNS/FQDN naming and provide cert SRV record details (target: Monday).
3) Marcus: create JIRA epic INF-2387 and initial sub-tasks: cert exchange, firewall rule signoff, cutover runbook, test harness.
4) Camila: lead cutover window and coordinate on-call rotation.

I'll create INF-2387 now and link it here. Please add your acceptance criteria to the ticket and I will split into proper sub-tasks.

On the routing question: control.redwood-internal.global will be reachable over the same peering path as inference traffic for this deployment; we will not require a separate management VPC. We will, however, tag control plane traffic so customers can filter it separately on their side if they prefer.

Thanks — happy to take the call tomorrow.

Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
